You said Do you have the time? 第五題

Do you have the time? 第五題

第五題的正確答案是 (C)。

這題考的是 the 的有無所帶來的語意差異：

Do you have the time?
加上定冠詞 the，意思是「你知道現在幾點嗎？」（等同於 What time is it?）。
因此回答時間最符合語境："Yes, it's ten thirty."（是的，現在十點半。）

Do you have time?（沒有 the）
意思是「你有空嗎？」（time 為不可數名詞，指空閒時間）。
如果題目問的是這句，回答 (B) I'm free 才是正確的。

You said 第25題請翻譯成白話文。

第25題請翻譯成白話文。

第 25 題的題目與選項白話翻譯如下：

題目：
What is the main idea of this reading?
→ 這篇文章的主旨（主要在講什麼）是什麼？

選項：

(A) Service industry is the only place that follows omotenashi.
→ 服務業是唯一落實「款待精神（omotenashi）」的地方。
(文章提到其他地方也有，且「唯一 only」通常過於極端)

(B) The spirit of omotenashi should live on in Japan.
→ 款待精神應該在日本一直傳承／延續下去。
(對應文章第三段提到成立組織就是為了 "keep the idea of omotenashi alive"，讓這份精神持續實踐與發揚)

(C) Omotenashi is thought to be important by visitors in Japan.
→ 款待精神被來到日本的訪客認為很重要。
(文章主要是從日本服務者、推廣組織的角度談精神核心，並非強調「遊客覺得它重要」)

(D) The role of waiters and waitresses in Japanese restaurants.
→ 日本餐廳服務生所扮演的角色。
(服務生只是第二段用來說明款待精神的一個例子，不是整篇文章的核心大意)

正確答案為：(B)

You said 請將這一段文章逐句翻譯成白話文。

請將這一段文章逐句翻譯成白話文。

這裡為您逐句翻譯這篇閱讀測驗的全文：

【第一段】

When eating out in Japan, you may be familiar with a custom known as “omotenashi.”

在日本外出用餐時，你可能對一種被稱為「omotenashi（おもてなし，款待）」的習俗很熟悉。

The word means “Japanese hospitality.”

這個詞的意思是「日式熱情款待」。

You can always feel it when you are in Japan.

當你人在日本時，總能時時刻刻感受到它。

But what does it mean?

但它究竟代表什麼意思呢？

【第二段】

The heart of omotenashi lies in the active yet careful manner in which Japanese waiters and waitresses try to pay attention to and meet diners’ needs without being too obvious.

款待精神的核心，在於日本服務人員主動卻又細心的方式——他們會留意並滿足用餐者的需求，同時又不會表現得太過刻意。

They even fulfill diners’ needs before they ask for them.

他們甚至會在客人開口要求之前，就先一步滿足客人的需求。

Greetings and conversations should always be nice and polite.

打招呼與談話問候時，總是要親切而且有禮貌。

Food must be presented beautifully.

餐點擺盤呈現必須非常精美。

Tea cups should be refilled without the diners needing to ask, and so on.

茶杯不用等客人開口就該主動補滿，諸如此類等等。

【第三段（跨兩頁）】

To keep the idea of omotenashi alive, a group was started.

為了讓這種款待精神延續下去，有人成立了一個推廣團體。

This group has some main goals to keep the art of omotenashi under practicing.

這個團體有一些主要目標，是為了讓這項「款待的藝術」能持續被實踐。

They want people to feel welcome, make sure eating out is enjoyable, show off Japan’s great food, and also have fun.

他們希望讓大家感受到賓至如歸的歡迎、確保外出用餐是令人享受的、展現日本的美食，同時大家也能樂在其中。

These ideas aren't [just for restaurants; they also apply to...] hot springs, and big stores.

(結合文意接續至第二張圖開頭)

這些理念不只是為了餐廳，也適用於溫泉旅館以及大型商店。

Why not visit Japan and experience omotenashi for yourself?

何不親自造訪日本，體驗看看這種款待精神呢？

You said 可 以 朗 讀 這 一 段 。 文 章 嗎 ?

可 以 朗 讀 這 一 段 。 文 章 嗎 ?

When eating out in Japan, you may be familiar with a custom known as "omotenashi." The word means "Japanese hospitality." You can always feel it when you are in Japan. But what does it mean?

The heart of omotenashi lies in the active yet careful manner in which Japanese waiters and waitresses try to pay attention to and meet diners' needs without being too obvious. They even fulfill diners' needs before they ask for them. Greetings and conversations should always be nice and polite. Food must be presented beautifully. Tea cups should be refilled without the diners needing to ask, and so on.

To keep the idea of omotenashi alive, a group was started. This group has some main goals to keep the art of omotenashi under practicing. They want people to feel welcome, make sure eating out is enjoyable, show off Japan's great food, and also have fun. These ideas aren't hot springs and big stores. Why not visit Japan and experience omotenashi for yourself?

You said 還 在 精 神

還 在 精 神

When eating out in Japan, you may be familiar with a custom known as "omotenashi." The word means "Japanese hospitality." You can always feel it when you are in Japan. But what does it mean?

The heart of omotenashi lies in the active yet careful manner in which Japanese waiters and waitresses try to pay attention to and meet diners' needs without being too obvious. They even fulfill diners' needs before they ask for them. Greetings and conversations should always be nice and polite. Food must be presented beautifully. Tea cups should be refilled without the diners needing to ask, and so on.

To keep the idea of omotenashi alive, a group was started. This group has some main goals to keep the art of omotenashi under practicing. They want people to feel welcome, make sure eating out is enjoyable, show off Japan's great food, and also have fun. These ideas aren't hot springs and big stores. Why not visit Japan and experience omotenashi for yourself?
